subject: SummitLane hosted API: traffic slab & $/1M token targets — follow-up
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@summitlane.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: SummitLane hosted API: traffic slab & $/1M token targets — follow-up

Hi Samir / Nina —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good conversation and helpful context on peak user flows. Per our call I wanted to capture the traffic shape and the questions we'll need answered to put together a concrete hosted pricing proposal. I left a few inline asks below so we can align quickly.

Quick recap of what we learned on the call:
- Primary use: real-time customer chat + short-context retrieval (avg prompt ~650 tokens, response ~320 tokens).
- Expected production start: Q4 pilot; GA in mid next year if pilot metrics look good.
- Hard SLO: 95% of chat requests should return <300ms server-side latency (Redwood can route to lower-latency variants during peak).

Numbers we need from you (please reply inline or attach a sample export):
1) Typical monthly active users and expected messages per user (we need to translate to tokens/month).
2) Peak TPS you see during flash events today (or a 99th percentile QPS over busiest 15-min window).
3) Any regulatory constraints that require Private deployment or dedicated pools.

What we'll produce after we get the numbers:
- Pricing bands with target $/1M tokens for baseline and peak-safe tiers.
- Suggested commit slab (monthly tokens) + burst/auto-burst policy to hit your latency targets while optimizing unit economics.
- Draft SOW and pilot success criteria (I attached the sample SOW template).

Attachments: SOW_draft_v1.pdf (SOW template), sample usage CSV (optional if you have it).

Next steps: can you send the last 30 days of token counts by day (or the attached CSV), plus a rough peak TPS estimate? Once we have that I'll loop in engineering for a short call to validate latency assumptions.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

From: Samir Patel <samir@summitlane.ai>

Cc: Nina Rao <nina@clientsummit.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SummitLane hosted API: traffic slab & $/1M token targets — follow-up

Vanessa —
Appreciate the clear recap. Attaching our last 30 days export (summitlane_q1_usage.csv) — it's daily token totals plus peak-second and 15-min rolling peak TPS we capture at our edge. High-level answers here while you review the file:

- Monthly token run-rate (current production): ~28M tokens/month.
- Pilot target (Q4): expect to grow to ~85–110M tokens/month assuming feature rollout.
- Flash events: we typically see short spikes to ~420 TPS (15-min rolling 99th ~270 TPS).
- Avg tokens/request: about 980 total (prompt + response); majority are under 1,200.
- Compliance: SOC2 in progress; no air-gapped requirement for pilot.

Notes:
- We would like a pricing illustration that keeps baseline <$80 per 1M tokens for the committed band and shows the delta for peak-protected capacity (i.e., burst cushion).
- We can accept a 3-month pilot commitment for initial performance validation.

Attaching CSV now. Let us know if you want the raw logs instead of daily aggregates.

Thanks —
Samir
VP Product, SummitLane
[sent from mobile]

[attachment: summitlane_q1_usage.csv (CSV, 58 KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 18:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SummitLane hosted API: traffic slab & $/1M token targets — follow-up

Vanessa — quick internal notes after looking at the CSV Samir sent:

- Daily token math checks out: current 28M/mo -> pilot band (~100M/mo) is plausible with the growth they're projecting.
- Peak profile: 420 TPS observed is meaningful; for hosted API we should recommend a two-tier approach:
  * Committed slab: price at target $/1M (baseline) sized to their expected steady-state (we'd propose ~60–80M/mo).
  * Peak protection: either a burst cushion that triggers to higher-cost per-token burn or a percentage of reserved burst capacity (SLA-backed) for sustained peak windows.
- Latency SLO: to meet 95% <300ms we need to size fallback variants and KV caching; that'll push engineering config but is feasible.

Pricing sketch to propose to Samir: baseline $/1M = $78 (for a 60–80M commit), burst price (on-demand) = $120/1M for tokens consumed above commit during peak windows. Also show blended price for 100M commit.

I'll prepare a short ops note with inferred GPU footprints so we can justify the bands to finance.

Karthik
Sr Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>

Samir — thanks for the export and the numbers, that helps a lot.

Immediate next steps (from our side):
- I'll send a short written pricing memo by EOD Monday with three bands: conservative (40–60M commit), mid (60–95M commit), and aggressive (95–120M commit). Each band will include:
  • target $/1M tokens for the committed tier,
  • burst/on-demand per-1M rate, and
  • expected blended $/1M at the mid-point.

- Karthik will attach an ops appendix that maps the mid (60–95M) band to expected peak handling and what burst cushion is required to hit the 95% <300ms latency SLO.

Housekeeping ask for you (can you confirm by reply):
- Do you expect the 420 TPS spikes to be multi-region or concentrated in a single region?
- Any blackout windows (e.g., marketing sends) we should be aware of for auto-burst sizing?

I'll also draft a short pilot SOW (2–3 week performance validation) and send a DocuSign link once you agree to the commit band.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
